title: Interleaved refresh leading to temporary privilege suppression for rotated API keys
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent 403s during rolling upgrades and node failovers. Root cause appears to be interleaved token refreshes across parallel request paths that produced a short-lived state where a newly rotated API key became orphaned (accepted by the auth proxy but not yet reconciled across serving nodes), which suppressed privileges for active sessions for ~5-30s. This manifested as transient ‘insufficient scope’ errors and customer escalations to Support.

Observed impact:
- Multiple customers on Dedicated pools and one Private on-prem trial experienced brief request failures for control-plane API and inference endpoints.
- Errors concentrated during capacity failover, node drain, and key rotation windows.
- Business impact: customer-facing outages for a small subset of high-traffic flows; Support opened P1 escalations.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Token refresh is not completely atomic across the gateway and the per-node cache reconciliation path.
- A race between: (A) issuing rotated credentials and marking the old key revoked, (B) concurrent request handlers that read stale namespace bindings from local fast caches, and (C) the background reconciler applying the rotated key lineage. When (A) occurs slightly out-of-order with (B), the request reaches a node that accepts the new signature but still looks up privileges via the old cache entry which has been marked revoked elsewhere, so the request is denied.

Reproduction steps (dev/staging):
1) Start a dedicated pool with two serving nodes and enable short rotation TTLs in staging.
2) Create an API key, bind to org X, issue steady high-rate requests from a client session.
3) Trigger a rotation and simultanously drain one node (simulate failover).
4) Observe intermittent 403s for a subset of requests hitting the drained node while rotation propagation is in flight.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Support temporarily extended rotation grace window for affected customers and disabled aggressive background reconciliation in the affected zone.
- Deployed a canary server-side guard that accepts the new key if it presents a valid lineage token for the last 60s (hotfix PR merged to staging).

Longer-term fix plan:
1) Make key swap atomic at the gateway layer by using a refresh-lineage token and a one-way reconciliation handshake.
2) Add idempotent refresh endpoints that return canonical key lineage id and epoch to callers so parallel flows can coordinate.
3) Harden per-node cache reconciliation to apply rotation deltas instead of full revokes during a rotation window.
4) Add end-to-end tests that exercise simultaneous rotation + drain scenarios and assert no 403s.
5) Roll out runtime-1.19 with the atomics and reconciliation changes behind a feature flag and progressively enable for Dedicated pools.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproduction no longer exhibits 403s in 100k simulated rotation+drain requests.
- Observability added: per-key lineage metric, rotation lag histogram, and per-route 403 spike alert.
- Post-deploy customer validation on one Dedicated pool for 48h with no regressions.

Notes/links:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876
- Postmortem draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Token+Refresh+Race+Postmortem
- Incident dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/board/incident/refresh-race-25690
